Scientific referencesRajagopalan et al., JCI 2020 · Zhang et al., Science 2025 · Nakamya et al., IJMS 2025


This is a defense-style presentation of completed computational work, not a claim of a new animal experiment or independent biological replication. “New” means added by this project, not proven biological novelty. The analyses and reference outputs were completed on 18–20 October 2026; this presentation was prepared on 28 October 2026. title: Air pollution and mouse brain omics
section: Brain regions and exposure designs define the question
text:
Brain regions and exposure designs define the question

01 / Context

Regional RNA measurements can identify expression associations under a particular route, dose, genotype and age.
The project addresses three linked questions:

Can the deposited author analyses be reconstructed?
What do explicitly specified reanalyses and response-interaction tests show?
Where are prioritized transcripts detected in an independent measured brain reference?


Scientific referencesRajagopalan et al., JCI 2020 · Zhang et al., Science 2025 · Nakamya et al., IJMS 2025


The background is deliberately brief. The four primary papers motivate hypothalamic, cortical and hippocampal questions involving particulate matter and ozone, but their routes and units are not interchangeable. An exposure association in bulk tissue may reflect regulation, tissue composition, source-quality variation or combinations of these. Spatial reference anatomy helps locate baseline detection, but cannot identify which individual cells responded in the original experiment. This presentation prioritizes the computational evidence and the limits needed to defend each inference.

This slide prevents pseudoreplication. Thousands of cells do not replace independent exposed and control animals. The spatial folds are useful for checking prediction at unsampled reference sections, but they cannot validate across donors or exposures. title: Air pollution and mouse brain omics
section: Bulk contrasts and spatial cells answer different questions
text:
Bulk contrasts and spatial cells answer different questions

01 / Context

Exposure comparison. Bulk RNA-seq combines RNA from many cells in each sampled region. The animal supplies the independent replicate. A regional difference can reflect expression within cells, changes in cellular composition, or both.
Spatial reference. MERFISH counts a targeted gene panel at measured cell positions in one unexposed donor. It shows where a transcript is detected in that reference.
Connection. We map regional candidates onto the measured panel. The atlas supplies anatomical context, while the separate exposure experiment supplies the regional contrast.

Scientific referencesRajagopalan et al., JCI 2020 · Zhang et al., Science 2025 · Zhang et al., Nature 2023


The atlas and exposure studies have different animals, assays and estimands. Spatial cells cannot be assigned the pollution label of an animal from another experiment. Increasing the number of reference cells improves description within the donor but does not increase the number of exposed biological replicates. The measured panel also limits which regional candidates can appear on a spatial map. Missing panel genes remain missing rather than receiving invented coordinates or expression.

title: Air pollution and mouse brain omics
section: Fosb across the experimental and spatial analyses
text:
Fosb across the experimental and spatial analyses

01 / Context

Regional evidence. The eight-animal ACA comparison estimates higher Fosb RNA after PM exposure. Its shrunken log₂ fold change is +0.99711, corresponding to a 1.996-fold multiplier.
Measured reference. The separate atlas detects Fosb in 1,418 of 14,582 ACA cells. Original coordinates place these detections within the registered anatomy.
Illustrative display. Multiplying every reference value by 1.996 changes the color and magnitude while preserving positions and measured zeros. This assumption illustrates the regional estimate without identifying the cells that actually respond to PM.

Scientific referencesZhang et al., Science 2025 · Zhang et al., Nature 2023 · Love et al., Genome Biol. 2014


Fosb is a concrete example linking the project’s primary count analysis, measured panel and viewer. The primary model uses four PBS and four PM animals. The atlas denominator is all measured ACA cells, including measured zeros, and comes from one unexposed donor. A positive bulk coefficient does not imply activation in every Fosb-positive cell. Protein abundance, AP-1 activity, isoform-specific FosB versus ΔFosB effects and causal mechanisms are outside what the gene-level RNA measurement establishes.

title: Air pollution and mouse brain omics
section: Numerical recovery and independent biological validation
text:
Numerical recovery and independent biological validation

02 / Methods

Numerical recovery asks whether the same deposited inputs and analysis rules recover the authors’ effects, probabilities and selected genes. Cortex recovers all four tested significant-gene sets exactly.
Methodological sensitivity asks what changes when a model, filter or analytical population changes. Hypothalamic reconstruction remains incomplete because key RUVg specifications are unavailable.
Independent biological validation would require additional animals or experiments. Reanalyzing the source animals, even with another software package, checks computation and assumptions while leaving the biological sample size unchanged.

Scientific referencesZhang et al., Science 2025 · Rajagopalan et al., JCI 2020


Identical gene counts alone are a weak reproduction criterion because different sets can have the same size. The cortex comparison also checks identities, effect estimates, p values and selected-set Jaccard. This is strong evidence for recovery of the checked count-level output, not validation of every experiment in the source article. Source metadata concerns remain relevant even when calculations match. Transparent nonagreement and explicit missing specifications are scientific results of a reproduction audit rather than reasons to tune an analysis until it matches.

The paper describes lane normalization, empirical controls and RUVg before downstream testing.

The exact 5,000 negative-control genes and unwanted-factor count k are unavailable.

title: Air pollution and mouse brain omics
section: Normalization and dispersion in the count model
text:
Normalization and dispersion in the count model

02 / Methods

Normalization accounts for technical differences in the amount of RNA sequenced. Otherwise, a deeply sequenced library could appear higher for many genes even without a biological change. Ozone also uses effective-length information from transcript quantification.
Dispersion describes variation among animals beyond ordinary count noise. A variable gene needs a larger, more consistent group difference to supply strong evidence.
The coefficient estimates the chosen regional comparison after these adjustments. Neither normalization nor dispersion estimation creates biological replicates or removes an unmeasured source of confounding.

Scientific referencesLove et al., Genome Biol. 2014 · Muzellec et al. 2023 · Soneson et al. 2015


DESeq2 and PyDESeq2 use negative-binomial count models with gene-specific dispersion estimation and information sharing. For the simple PM comparisons the normalization factor reduces to sample-specific size factors. The tximport ozone workflow adds gene/sample normalization from effective lengths, so a single library-size description would be incomplete. These count procedures do not apply to the signed, deposited miRNA continuous signals, which use limma. Low counts generally limit precision, and a retained zero remains an observation rather than a missing value filled by normalization.

title: Air pollution and mouse brain omics
section: Effect size, uncertainty and the discovery threshold
text:
Effect size, uncertainty and the discovery threshold

02 / Methods

Effect size describes direction and magnitude. A log₂ fold change of +1 corresponds to twice the regional RNA level, while −1 corresponds to half, under the fitted contrast.
The standard error and Wald test compare the estimated effect with its sampling uncertainty. A large fold change from inconsistent animals may have weak evidence.
BH adjustment evaluates many genes as a declared testing family. A nominal p < 0.05 can become q ≥ 0.05. Shrinkage stabilizes displayed effect estimates, while the stated inferential model determines the reported tests.

Scientific referencesLove et al., Genome Biol. 2014 · Zhu et al. 2019


BH q values should not be described as the posterior probability that an individual gene is false. Under its assumptions, the procedure controls the expected false-discovery proportion among rejections at the chosen level. A pointwise 95% Wald interval is an approximate interval for one model coefficient, not a simultaneous interval for all genes or a per-cell interval. Different filtering populations and multiplicity families can change the discovery list even when underlying effects are similar. The MLE and shrunken effects are retained separately throughout the project.

text:
Interaction tests compare exposure effects directly

02 / Methods

Within a stratum, the model compares ozone with filtered air at one starting age and APOE genotype. Each stratum has only three animals per exposure group.
An interaction asks whether the ozone effect itself differs between ages or genotypes, using coefficient differences and their covariance. One significant stratum and one nonsignificant stratum do not answer that question.
Here, the joint age-dependent exposure LRT identifies eight genes under its own BH family, and one under BH pooled across the three joint heterogeneity tests. The conclusion depends on the stated test and family.

Scientific referencesNakamya et al., IJMS 2025 · Love et al., Genome Biol. 2014


The 24 RNA-seq samples form the eight age×genotype×exposure combinations with three animals each. The full factorial design has eight parameters and estimates all groups jointly. The four-degree-of-freedom exposure LRT and the two-degree-of-freedom age-dependent exposure LRT test different null hypotheses. Signed individual interaction contrasts also differ from the joint LRTs. Starting ages of three and seventeen months are source design labels at exposure onset. These labels should not be relabeled as terminal sampling ages.

Bayesian detection: methods
For gene gg, anatomy aa and physical section ss, YsagY_{sag} is the number of positive raw imaging counts among nsan_{sa} measured cells, including all zeros in the denominator. We use
Ysag∣psag∼Binomial⁡(nsa,psag),psag∣μag,κag∼Beta⁡(μagκag,(1−μag)κag).
Y_{sag}\mid p_{sag}\sim\operatorname{Binomial}(n_{sa},p_{sag}),\qquad
p_{sag}\mid\mu_{ag},\kappa_{ag}\sim\operatorname{Beta}(\mu_{ag}\kappa_{ag},(1-\mu_{ag})\kappa_{ag}).

The beta-binomial marginal likelihood allows section-to-section heterogeneity, rather than treating all cells as independent replicates sharing one fixed probability. Proper independent priors are μ∼Beta⁡(0.5,0.5)\mu\sim\operatorname{Beta}(0.5,0.5) and ln⁡κ∼𝒩(ln⁡20,1.52)\ln\kappa\sim\mathcal N(\ln20,1.5^2). These choices are fixed; they do not use held-out expression. Integration uses a deterministic 64 × 48 prior-quantile grid, with grid sensitivity reported separately. Hypermean intervals use weighted discrete-grid quantiles. Known-section probability and held-out positive-count intervals use 8,192 fixed-seed mixture draws; full-reference new-section probability intervals use deterministic inversion of the weighted Beta-mixture CDF. This is numerical grid/Monte Carlo integration, not an exact continuous posterior or an MCMC convergence claim. (SciPy developers, n.d.) Section propensities are exchangeable within each anatomy and gene; this model does not separate biological AP trends from technical section variation.
Increasing the integration grid from 64 × 48 to 96 × 64 changes full-reference posterior mean probabilities by at most 0.00020 in ACA and 0.00054 in HY. New-section probability interval endpoints change by at most 0.0026 and 0.0036, respectively; discrete hypermean interval endpoints can move by about 0.020 and 0.018. Held-out count coverage changes from 97.89% to 98.05% in ACA and stays at 99.35% in HY. These checks describe finite numerical precision; high coverage with wide intervals does not establish predictive usefulness.
The known-section posterior probability uses that reference section’s observed numerator and denominator. It is a fitted estimate, not held-out prediction. Its credible interval differs from uncertainty in the anatomical hypermean μ\mu, and from the distinct distribution of a new section’s probability. New-section positive-count predictive intervals condition on the actual held-out denominator nn. These are probabilities or counts of detection, not expression magnitudes or spatially inferred molecules.
The same five whole-section folds and neighboring guard sections used below provide out-of-sample evaluation. A regional nonanatomical model is trained on the same permitted sections for comparison. Brier loss is a cell-weighted descriptive prediction score; positive-count interval coverage is reported over section–anatomy groups, with denominators and prior-only groups explicit. A held-out anatomy absent from training retains the specified prior and is not silently replaced with a learned anatomical pattern.

Spatial-expression baseline: methods

Data, target and anatomical information
All registered anterior-cingulate and hypothalamic cells from the unexposed male ABCA-2 donor are retained. Ten previously selected measured genes per region are modeled. Counts and coordinates remain unchanged. The response is natural-log transformed imaging count, yig=ln⁡(1+cig)y_{ig}=\ln(1+c_{ig}), including measured zeros. It is not log₂ fold change, RNA-seq normalized expression, or a protein measurement. (Zhang et al. 2023)
Anatomical substructures, standardized CCF coordinates and a finite anisotropic radial-basis expansion describe the spatial mean. The model can represent jumps between anatomical categories. Original section intercepts absorb slice-wide shifts. Expression-derived cell-class and subclass labels are excluded from the primary predictors, avoiding target information carried through atlas RNA-based annotations. Physical-section identities define the validation partitions.


Proper priors and posterior distributions
For each gene, the working model is
yig=ϕ(𝒓i,ai)⊤𝜷g+δs(i),g+ϵig,ϵig∼𝒩(0,σg2).
y_{ig}=\phi(\mathbf r_i,a_i)^\top\boldsymbol\beta_g+\delta_{s(i),g}+\epsilon_{ig},
\qquad \epsilon_{ig}\sim\mathcal N(0,\sigma_g^2).

Here 𝒓i\mathbf r_i denotes registered position, aia_i anatomical category and s(i)s(i) physical section. Coefficients and section effects have proper zero-centered Normal priors conditional on residual variance, with a proper inverse-Gamma prior for that variance. The Normal–Inverse-Gamma update yields Student-t posterior distributions after integrating coefficient and variance uncertainty. Anisotropy, prior strengths, nuisance variance and basis size are fixed for the primary analysis; sensitivity fits vary prespecified alternatives.
The map displays the spatial mean with the section offset averaged to zero. Two uncertainty quantities have different meanings:

The 95% latent-mean credible interval describes uncertainty about that section-adjusted mean under the model.
The 95% new-cell/new-section predictive interval also includes residual variation and an unseen section offset. This wider interval is evaluated against held-out measured cells.

The Gaussian likelihood is a working approximation for sparse transformed counts. It can assign probability below zero, outside the physical support of ln⁡(1+c)\ln(1+c). Negative fitted means, negative bounds and predictive mass below zero are retained and diagnosed. Estimates are not exponentiated into claims of expected molecule counts. Interval uncertainty is conditional on the chosen anatomy, basis, priors and registration; it does not include all biological or registration uncertainty.


Whole-section validation
Five contiguous blocks of physical sections are reserved in turn. Neighboring guard sections are excluded from training. Anatomy levels, coordinate scaling and basis locations are learned from training cells only; held-out expression does not determine them. All test cells remain together with their original section. Final maps fitted to all reference cells are clearly distinguished from these out-of-sample predictions.
Each gene is compared with a training-only anatomy-mean model and simple spatial nearest-neighbor interpolation. The retained metrics include RMSE, MAE, predictive-interval coverage and width, with observed zero and positive-count behavior examined separately. Fixed alternative spatial scales and shrinkage strengths assess dependence on priors. Test results are not used to rename an unsuccessful model as validated.
One donor supports within-donor spatial prediction, not independent animal replication, cross-donor performance or generalization to exposure. Whole-section blocking reduces local information leakage but does not eliminate all spatial dependence or model misspecification.

The following results report prediction accuracy and calibration, including failures. A successful implementation/data check does not establish scientific calibration or superiority over a baseline.

title: Bayesian detection and spatial baseline validation
text:
Interpretation and limits
A finer display grid, smoother field or narrow conditional credible interval does not increase the acquisition resolution. Predictions at existing positions do not create cells in the approximately 200 µm gaps between sampled sections, and this model generates no extra cells or hemisphere. Reliable resolution enhancement would require independent measurements demonstrating recovery of that additional detail.
No cell-type-specific PM2.5 response is fitted here. Baseline spatial priors and regional bulk changes cannot uniquely identify such responses. The original PM2.5 3D scenario retains its uniform regional multiplier. Posterior baseline uncertainty is not an exposure-effect interval.

How genes were selected and annotated
The hypothalamic discovery list is the complete original Python BH < 0.05 set. Cortex priorities are the first 20 protein-coding genes ordered by primary BH q, then the documented tie-breaks. Gene names link to the corresponding NCBI source; available protein records link to UniProt. A molecular function describes the annotated gene product. Differential RNA abundance does not itself measure protein abundance, enzyme activity, or a pathway’s activation.
Effects in the tables are unshrunken regional MLE log₂FC with pointwise 95% Wald intervals. BH q refers to the original primary test. The 3D central scenario uses the separately saved shrunken coefficient; the two estimates are not interchangeable.

title: Functional enrichment: GO Biological Process
text:
Two classical gene-set approaches summarize completed gene-level RNA-seq contrasts. Overrepresentation analysis (ORA) asks whether an annotation occurs more often among FDR-selected genes than expected in the mapped testable gene universe. Preranked gene-set enrichment analysis (GSEA) asks whether genes belonging to a set tend to accumulate toward either end of the complete quality-eligible signed Wald-statistic ranking. The approaches use different inputs and different multiplicity procedures, so agreement is informative but is not required. (Ashburner et al. 2000; Subramanian et al. 2005; Fang et al. 2023)
The PM hypothalamus and cortex comparisons are kept separate. The four ozone age-by-genotype contrasts are added only after their corresponding Wald tables are complete. These are six possible contrast entries, not six exchangeable cohorts. No gene lists, animals, p values, or causal claims are pooled across brain regions, exposure agents, or experimental protocols. The unsigned global ozone LRT and miRNA array features are not supplied as signed mRNA rankings.

Interpretation: GO terms overlap and share ancestors. A large number of significant term labels does not represent the same number of independent mechanisms. GSEA’s gene-set permutations do not capture biological-replicate uncertainty or preserve gene–gene correlations. Enrichment is exploratory evidence about ranked or selected gene sets, rather than proof of pathway activation, suppression, or a cell-specific pollutant mechanism.

title: Functional enrichment: GO Biological Process
text:
Materials and methods

Mouse annotation, mapping, and reproducibility
Gene sets are built from the downloaded mouse MGI GAF and GO Basic ontology, with source URLs, release-header dates, checksums, and derived GMT provenance retained. Their individual source dates are preserved; they should not be treated as a newly generated matched annotation release. Only positive mouse Biological Process annotations are used. NOT annotations are excluded, while positive annotation evidence codes, including electronic evidence, are retained.
Term memberships propagate through active is_a and part_of Biological Process ancestors. Regulatory edges and cross-aspect relations are not used for propagation. Alternative IDs and obsolete terms resolve only when an unambiguous active replacement is available. (Ashburner et al. 2000)
Mapping uses case-sensitive canonical mouse symbols or uniquely resolving GAF synonyms. It does not uppercase genes, infer human orthologs, or match free-text gene descriptions. When several DE features map to one symbol, the representative is selected by the highest baseMean, with lexical feature-ID tie-breaking, independently of effect direction and significance. Ambiguous and unmapped symbols remain visible in the mapping audit.


ORA background, foreground, and FDR
The ORA universe comprises unique mapped representative genes with a finite adjusted DE p value. Mapped genes without a specific GO-BP annotation remain in the universe. Higher- and lower-expression foregrounds use gene-level DE FDR < 0.05 and the sign of the original unshrunken coefficient, without an additional effect-size threshold.
Eligible GO terms have 15–500 members after intersection with the contrast-specific universe. A one-sided hypergeometric survival probability tests the observed or greater overlap. Terms with zero overlap remain in the tested family with p = 1. BH correction is applied across the entire eligible term family, separately for each contrast and each direction. ORA’s padj_BH is therefore distinct from a gene-level DE adjusted p value. (Benjamini and Hochberg 1995)


Preranked GSEA and gene-test quality
The ranking includes unique mapped representatives with both a finite unshrunken Wald statistic and a finite unshrunken-test p value after the source analysis’s validity checks. A finite statistic alone is insufficient: Cook-filtered or otherwise unreliable tests can retain a numerical statistic while having an unavailable p value. These rows are excluded from GSEA, and the exclusions are exported. For ozone, the source analysis also withholds tests for nonconverged fits and genes with zero counts in all six animals of the corresponding stratum. The pre-filter audit p values are not substituted for those unavailable valid-test p values. This is a gene-test quality decision, not an exclusion of an animal.
Genes that have a finite unshrunken-test p value but a missing adjusted p value because of independent filtering remain eligible for ranking. This applies to the PM analyses where that filtering was enabled; ozone uses a fixed count prefilter without adaptive independent filtering. No gene-level FDR or fold-change threshold selects the ranked genes. Genes are ordered by descending signed statistic, with gene-symbol tie-breaking. Term membership is additionally restricted to 15–500 genes in the resulting rank. (Subramanian et al. 2005; Fang et al. 2023)
GSEApy uses 1,000 gene-set/gene-label permutations, weight 1, and seed 20261018. These are not phenotype-label permutations. The reported fdr_qvalue is the GSEA algorithmic normalized-enrichment-score FDR estimate, not BH correction. A nominal permutation p value or estimated q value of zero is a finite-permutation result and does not mean zero error probability.

title: Functional enrichment: GO Biological Process
text:
Biological interpretation
Positive NES denotes association toward the higher-expression end of the specific exposure contrast; negative NES denotes association toward the lower-expression end. Neither sign establishes biochemical pathway activity or the cell population responsible. The same genes can contribute to many related GO terms, and annotation coverage is unequal across genes. Classical ORA does not explicitly model gene-length or detectability biases; the testable background limits, but does not remove, those concerns.
The molecular models and sample sizes remain those of the original regional experiments. An apparent shared term across cortex, hypothalamus, or an ozone stratum is a hypothesis for targeted comparison, not a pooled causal estimate. Cell composition, sampling, age, genotype, exposure delivery, and technical differences can contribute to apparent convergence. No validated target map is supplied for the miRNA array, so mRNA GO analysis is not inferred from miRNA identifiers.

text:
Materials and methods

Input, annotation, and measurement scale
The GEO series matrix contains 1,268 feature rows. The GPL17912 platform table maps biological mouse miRNA probes to the supplied miRNA_ID labels. Historical platform identifiers are retained without a silent miRBase update or aggregation. Twenty-one control or unannotated rows are preserved in the source export but excluded from differential analysis. Two biological miRNA rows, mmu-miR-3963 and mmu-miR-6366, have zero variance across the nine samples and are also excluded.
GEO describes quantile normalization with GeneSpring but does not explicitly establish the log2 measurement scale of the deposited matrix. The supplied values include negative values and a large lower-bound pile-up. The analysis applies neither a second log transform nor a count-data model. Effects are labeled mean differences in published normalized signal units, with positive values indicating higher signal in the PM group. They are not interpreted as log2 fold changes or converted to fold changes.

Statistical model and detection flags
Limma fits a three-group linear model with one group-mean coefficient for saline, 1 mg/kg PM, and 5 mg/kg PM. The two planned contrasts compare each PM group with saline. Empirical Bayes moderation uses trend=True and robust=False; the optional omnibus test is a two-coefficient moderated F test for the two PM-minus-saline contrasts. (Ritchie et al. 2015)
Benjamini–Hochberg adjustment is applied across the retained miRNA rows within each pairwise contrast, and separately within the omnibus test. These adjustments do not provide a single pooled FDR guarantee across the three test families. Exported standard errors and pointwise 95% moderated t intervals refer to the reported signal differences; the intervals are not simultaneous or multiplicity-adjusted. (Benjamini and Hochberg 1995)
The original Agilent detection calls are retained. A low-detection flag identifies rows with fewer than three Present calls in every group. These rows remain in the primary testing family, with their flag available for interpretation. No biological sample is removed on the basis of PCA. PCA uses the 500 most variable retained features, centered without variance scaling, on the deposited signal scale.

title: Introduction and study scope
text:
The cerebral cortex, hypothalamus, and hippocampus contain different mixtures of neurons, glia, vascular cells, and other cell populations. An expression signature measured in one region therefore addresses a different biological question from a signature measured elsewhere. Bulk tissue measurements also combine changes within cells with differences in the proportions or states of the cells contributing RNA. These distinctions matter when interpreting studies of air pollutants: an observed tissue signature can motivate a mechanistic hypothesis, but it does not identify the affected cell population or its anatomical position on its own.
The available experimental studies cover several complementary settings. Zhang and colleagues investigated air pollutants in a humanized alpha-synuclein mouse model and deposited anterior cingulate cortex RNA-seq data. Rajagopalan and colleagues examined metabolic responses to air pollution and reversibility, with hypothalamus among several sampled tissues. Ku and colleagues studied hippocampal miRNA expression after repeated PM2.5 aspiration. Nakamya and colleagues investigated hippocampal transcriptomic responses to ozone across age and APOE genotype groups. These studies provide region-specific starting points for secondary analysis rather than technical replicates of one experiment. (Zhang et al. 2025; Rajagopalan et al. 2020; Ku et al. 2017; Nakamya et al. 2025)

section: Matching the analysis to the assay
text:
Matching the analysis to the assay
RNA-seq count models and microarray signal models answer related questions on different measurement scales. The bulk RNA-seq analyses use count-based inference, retain original identifiers, and distinguish statistical testing from stabilized effect-size estimates. The miRNA analysis retains the deposited normalized signals and reports differences in those units because the deposited preprocessing description does not explicitly establish a log2 scale. Uncertainty, multiple testing, sample quality, and low-information features are reported alongside ranked results. (Love et al. 2014; Muzellec et al. 2023; Ritchie et al. 2015)

title: Introduction and study scope
text:
What the spatial atlas contributes
The Zhang 2023 whole-mouse-brain MERFISH atlas supplies a measured spatial reference from animals without an experimental pollutant exposure. Its targeted panel measures 1,122 genes and links individual segmented cells with anatomical coordinates and transferred transcriptomic annotations. This enables inspection of where a gene is normally detected and which annotated populations express it. It does not measure a pollutant response in the atlas animals. A projected bulk signature is therefore an inferred correspondence between experiments and reference tissue; it cannot establish exposure-induced expression changes in individual atlas cells. Genes outside the measured panel require a separately identified inference strategy. (Zhang et al. 2023)
The objective is to deliver reproducible classical omics analyses and a transparent spatial reference for follow-up. Each result is linked to its source matrix, sample selection, model, quality checks, and downloadable table. The report distinguishes completed comparisons from data that remain insufficient for a new exposure contrast, preserving a clear boundary between direct measurement, statistical estimation, and biological interpretation.

title: Introduction and study scope
text:
Questions and levels of evidence
The primary question is whether exposure is associated with regional expression differences under each original experimental design. A second question is whether ozone responses vary with age or APOE genotype; that requires direct interaction tests rather than comparing discovery counts. A third question asks whether the original authors’ numerical findings can be reconstructed from their deposits. These questions have different statistical units and validation criteria. Rajagopalan et al. (2020) Zhang et al. (2025) Ku et al. (2017) Nakamya et al. (2025)
The expanded report therefore places per-gene tests beside coordinated gene-set patterns, sample-level observations, uncertainty, and source-method comparisons. GO structure can generate mechanistic hypotheses but cannot establish pathway activity, cell identity, or a causal chain. A reproducible author result may still be sensitive to sample composition or unreported design variables. The reproduction audit records these distinctions explicitly.
The spatial question is narrower: where is a measured gene normally detected in the reference hypothalamus, and how would the same measured pattern change under a uniform regional bulk-effect scenario? The model neither reconstructs an exposed brain nor supplies exposed single cells. The 3D viewer retains this boundary while allowing anatomical exploration. Zhang et al. (2023)

title: Methods
text:
Source checks and preprocessing
Downloaded exposure files were checked against provider sizes and MD5 sums where available. The 49 spatial-reference files matched the Allen manifest in both size and MD5. Integer-valued, nonnegative counts, unique feature identifiers, sample order, group assignments, and gene-list agreement were checked before modeling. The seven hypothalamic files use a headerless whitespace-separated format and share the same 50,417 gene symbols in the same order. Negative values in the deposited miRNA signal matrix were retained because those values are already normalized continuous signals.
The cingulate-cortex matrix was matched to samples by the deposited library names, not the GEO sample order. The ambiguous alias in a PM-PFF-plus-PM sample is outside the eight-sample primary contrast and is not silently corrected. No batch, RIN, or individual age covariate was invented for the PM2.5 RNA-seq studies.

title: Methods
text:
Classical RNA-seq analysis

Hypothalamus and cingulate cortex
Counts were analyzed in Python using PyDESeq2, a Python implementation of the DESeq2 framework. Muzellec et al. (2023) Love et al. (2014) The hypothalamic filter required at least 10 counts in at least three of seven samples, retaining 19,611 genes. The cortex filter required at least 10 counts in at least four of eight samples, retaining 19,235 genes. Filters were applied before normalization and inferential modeling.
Each study was modeled separately with condition as the sole design factor and an explicit PM-versus-control contrast. Median-of-ratios size factors, gene-wise and trend-based dispersion estimation, negative-binomial generalized linear models, and two-sided Wald tests were used. Multiple-testing adjustment followed the implementation’s Benjamini–Hochberg procedure, with FDR < 0.05 as the primary threshold. Benjamini and Hochberg (1995) Cook’s filtering and independent filtering remain distinguished: missing adjusted p-values are not all attributed to outliers.
The original maximum-likelihood log₂ fold changes, errors, Wald statistics, p-values, and adjusted p-values were saved before apeglm shrinkage. Shrunken log₂ fold changes were retained separately for effect visualization and spatial scenarios; they do not replace the original hypothesis-test results. Zhu et al. (2019) A secondary threshold of absolute shrunken log₂FC ≥ 1 is reported descriptively in addition to FDR, without redefining the primary discovery set.


Sample quality and relationships
The report includes gene-assigned library depth, detected genes, normalized distributions, sample correlations/distances, and PCA. PCA uses the 500 most variable variance-stabilized genes, centered across samples without gene-variance scaling. Individual samples are labeled. No sample was removed to improve visual separation, no batch was inferred from a principal component, and no unrecorded batch correction was applied.
The hypothalamic variance-stabilizing transform uses the condition design when estimating the dispersion trend; the cortex and ozone exploratory transforms are blind to the design. This distinction is retained in the analysis provenance. It changes the transformation used for visualization, not the gene-level differential-expression contrast.


Hypothalamus sensitivity analysis
Because the hypothalamic PCA shows marked control heterogeneity, the complete analysis was refitted after omitting each of the seven samples in turn. The original primary gene universe was retained. Direction, effect magnitude, and FDR stability are reported for the eleven primary hits, and discovery counts are reported for every omission. These fits assess sensitivity; they do not select a preferred deletion or replace the seven-animal primary result.
An independent DESeq2 R fit checks implementation agreement using the same samples, gene filter, normalization, condition contrast, parametric dispersion trend, Cook’s settings, and finite-p hypothesis family. Original maximum-likelihood effects and standard errors are compared before shrinkage. Threshold crossings are reported without changing the prespecified Python primary analysis. This evaluates numerical sensitivity, not biological replication.

title: Methods
text:
Hippocampal miRNA analysis
GSE93967 was analyzed on its deposited quantile-normalized signal scale, without a second log transformation. GPL17912 probe annotations identify biological miRNA features and platform controls. Controls and constant biological rows were excluded; low-detection features were flagged and retained. Effects are mean differences in published signal units because a log₂ scale was not established from the deposit.
A three-group linear model was fit using the empirical-Bayes moderated statistics in limma. Ritchie et al. (2015) The 1 mg/kg-versus-control and 5 mg/kg-versus-control contrasts were tested separately, with Benjamini–Hochberg correction within each contrast family. An omnibus moderated F test describes differences across the three groups. Pointwise t-based intervals and all nine sample values remain available. mRNA Gene Ontology analysis was not applied to miRNA names without a validated target mapping.

title: Methods
text:
Ozone analysis from original reads
The 24 paired-end libraries are resolved from the source SDRF, keeping paired files together by ENA run. Initial raw quality and adapter content are assessed on the first 200,000 read pairs per library, explicitly a diagnostic subset rather than a complete-read quality audit. Full-run adapter-removal reports are retained. Adapter trimming is applied consistently when the documented criterion is met; no duplicate removal or arbitrary quality trimming is used.
Salmon quantification uses a fixed GENCODE M25/GRCm38 transcriptome plus the complete primary genome as decoys, automatic library-type inference, and sequence/GC bias correction. Provider checksums, reference-building steps, software versions, and per-library reports are stored with the workflow. Patro et al. (2017) Quantifications are imported at gene level with tximport, retaining effective-length information for DESeq2. Soneson et al. (2015) Mouse-reference quantification does not establish allele-specific human APOE expression.
The eight-group design crosses age, APOE genotype, and exposure, with three libraries per group. The full model includes the corresponding two-way and three-way interactions. Four ozone-versus-filtered-air contrasts describe the age/genotype strata. A likelihood-ratio test compares the full model with an age-by-genotype model, jointly testing the exposure-associated terms. Adjusted p-values are retained both within each stratum and across the family of four stratum contrasts. Inconsistent strain descriptions in the source metadata are documented rather than converted into an unsupported adjustment.

title: Methods
text:
Functional enrichment
Mouse Gene Ontology Biological Process associations are taken from a frozen official MGI GAF and go-basic OBO snapshot. NOT annotations are excluded, taxon is restricted to mouse, and eligible is-a/part-of ancestors are propagated. Exact current symbols and unambiguous source synonyms are distinguished; ambiguous aliases remain unmapped. Annotation versions, hashes, mapping decisions, and coverage are exported. Ashburner et al. (2000)
Over-representation analysis uses a one-sided hypergeometric test for higher- and lower-expression gene lists separately. The background comprises mapped, unique genes eligible for the original differential-expression test. Terms containing 15–500 background genes are tested. All eligible terms, including zero-overlap terms, enter the Benjamini–Hochberg correction within each direction-specific family. Lack of significant over-representation is reported directly.
Preranked GSEA uses finite signed Wald statistics with finite original p-values, excluding Cook-filtered nonfinite-p results while retaining finite-p genes that were independently filtered from adjusted-p reporting. It uses 1,000 gene-set permutations, a fixed seed, and 15–500-gene sets. Subramanian et al. (2005) Fang et al. (2023) Its algorithmic FDR is distinct from ORA’s BH adjustment. GSEA is exploratory here: overlapping terms and correlated genes are not independent mechanistic discoveries, and these analyses do not remove the small-sample and control-heterogeneity limitations.

title: Methods
section: Measured 3D reference and modeled PM2.5 scenario
text:
Measured 3D reference and modeled PM2.5 scenario
The spatial reference uses Zhuang-ABCA-2, an adult male donor. Cells are selected by the deposited CCF parcellation assignments to the hypothalamic division, matched by exact string cell identifiers to the measured H5AD matrix, and annotated by the atlas taxonomy. Zhang et al. (2023)


This selection contains 37,811 cells, 26 cell classes, and 49 hypothalamic substructures. All 1,122 measured genes are accessible; 1,003 have reliable bulk effect estimates. Cells are not subsampled, mirrored, or interpolated.


The viewer plots CCF millimeter distances as ML, AP, and −DV. It does not apply the centered NIfTI RAS affine to positive CCF coordinate distances. A voxel-label agreement check verifies the frame; boundary-level differences are retained. Anatomical surfaces are simplified to 0.15 mm for whole-brain context and 0.075 mm for the hypothalamus; the molecular coordinates themselves remain unchanged.
The central scenario is defined on the linear imaging-count scale:
Simulated value(cell, gene) = measured reference count(cell, gene)
                            × 2^(shrunken bulk PM-versus-FA log2 fold change)
The multiplier applies uniformly within the hypothalamus. Other regions provide anatomical context only and are not assigned an exposure effect. Alternative lower/upper scenarios use the unshrunken group coefficient ±1.96 standard errors; these are group-effect sensitivity scenarios, not single-cell confidence intervals.
The two views use identical cell positions, linked cameras, and a common log₂(1 + value) color scale. An optional common positive-value 99th-percentile cap is disclosed, with clipped color values retained in hover and source exports. Genes without reliable bulk inference remain reference-only; nonsignificant modeled genes carry an exploratory label.
The reference is not a matched control for the bulk study. Uniform transfer preserves basal gradients and zeros and does not identify cell-specific responses, altered abundance, migration, morphology, or exposed single-cell expression.

Descriptive atlas summaries
The measured reference is also summarized by each of its 26 classes and 49 substructures. Every measured gene retains its arithmetic mean linear imaging count, number of positive-count cells, and detection fraction within each group, including zeros in the denominator. Class composition and Tll1 detection plots are descriptive measurements from one donor. They do not include cell-level tests, confidence intervals or exposed-cell inference. The anatomical Tll1 plot displays the top 15 detection fractions among substructures with at least 100 selected cells; complete exports retain all 49 substructures. Measured-reference results.

title: Methods
text:
Reproducibility
Python source scripts, QMD notebooks, version records, original sample annotations, differential tables, normalized matrices, sensitivity fits, and SVG/PDF/PNG figure exports are retained in the repository. The miRNA backend uses R/limma and the ozone gene-level backend uses R/tximport/DESeq2, called from the Python workflow. No results are fabricated to fill unavailable spatial exposure measurements. Data and execution instructions.

title: Methods
text:
Expanded analyses and original-method recovery
The secondary-analysis chapter defines the nested interaction models, coefficient contrasts, correction families, figure-selection rules, and covariance-aware intervals. The reproduction chapter separately reconstructs the cortex five-group author model, hypothalamus method sensitivity, miRNA ANOVA/LSD candidates, and ozone author-table selection and candidate fits. These models do not replace the primary fits above. R 4.5.2, DESeq2 1.50.2, limma 3.66.0, and edgeR 4.8.2 sessions are exported with the corresponding results. Author-data downloads retain source hashes and URLs; publisher article text and artwork are excluded from the public site.

title: Methods
text:
Gene-centered priorities and encoded-product annotation
Primary hypothalamic FDR discoveries are retained in full. Cortex coding-gene priorities are selected from the fixed primary eight-animal result, ordered by unrounded BH q with declared tie-breaks. Separate top-ten lists require a measured MERFISH gene and eligible original effect estimates. Those selection groups remain distinct: only one hypothalamic measured candidate is a primary discovery, whereas the ten cortical measured priorities are significant. Selection after analysis supports description and follow-up, not independent confirmation.
Official NCBI mouse gene records and reviewed UniProt entries provide current symbols, gene type, protein products and molecular roles. Original assay symbols remain in the report. Confirmed aliases are documented separately; ambiguous aliases are not substituted. Noncoding RNA and pseudogene records do not receive a protein. A function inferred by similarity is not presented as an enzyme assay in these mice. RNA results do not distinguish unmeasured protein abundance or gene isoforms such as ΔFosB, Homer1a and XBP1s.

title: Methods
text:
Anterior cingulate cortex spatial extension
The same unexposed male Zhuang-ABCA-2 reference supplies all registered cells with division Isocortex and structure ACAd or ACAv, retaining all ten layer/substructure labels. ACA is an anatomical proxy for the reported dissection, whose exact surgical boundaries were not deposited. Exact cell IDs link coordinates and the raw measured H5AD matrix. The 14,582-cell reference is not subsampled, mirrored, or expression-imputed. Exact Ensembl identifiers map measured genes to the primary cortical result; a symbol difference is retained in provenance rather than resolved by invented substitution.
Each cortical gene’s measured imaging values are multiplied uniformly by 2 to the power of its primary cortical shrunken log₂FC. The cortical effect is restricted to ACA; hypothalamus retains its own independent bulk effect. The common reference/scenario scale is computed within each gene. A three-gene comparison reports observed detection and mean imaging counts including zeros, original regional RNA effects, BH q and annotation; it does not test between-gene exposure differences or equalize probe efficiencies.
The cortical atlas donor is not an experimental control for the humanized α-synuclein animals. Spatial location of a reference transcript and a regional effect do not identify which cells respond to PM2.5. Source coordinate/volume agreement, join invariants, count ranges and all 1,122 compressed gene vectors are checked numerically. See gene profiles and cortical 3D methods and results.

title: Methods
section: Sectional measurement and Bayesian spatial prediction
text:
Sectional measurement and Bayesian spatial prediction
The measured-section chapter joins original section metadata by exact cell ID and retains all registered ACA/HY cells and raw counts. Within-section experimental coordinates remain separate from CCF coordinates. Detection is positive raw count divided by all selected measured cells, including zeros; empty spatial bins are missing. ACA labels are layers/subdivisions, while HY labels are nuclei/subregions.
The Bayesian chapter gives the working likelihood, proper priors, section offsets, posterior targets, blocked whole-section validation, simple baselines and prior sensitivity. Model/data integrity and scientific performance are reported separately. The model is an unexposed-reference analysis and supplies no cell-type-specific pollutant effect or increase in measured acquisition resolution.

Differential expression and effect sizes
Genes must have at least 10 counts in at least four of the eight selected samples. PyDESeq2 fits a negative-binomial generalized linear model with design ~condition, median-of-ratios size factors, and a two-sided Wald contrast for PM relative to PBS. Benjamini–Hochberg adjusted p values target an FDR of 0.05 within this contrast, with independent filtering and Cook’s filtering enabled. The unshrunken maximum-likelihood coefficients, standard errors, Wald statistics, p values, and adjusted p values are saved before effect-size shrinkage. The additional shrunken coefficient and uncertainty columns use the apeGLM-style heavy-tailed shrinkage implemented by PyDESeq2. Shrinkage stabilizes effect-size displays; it does not replace the preserved Wald test results. (Zhu et al. 2019)
At four biological replicates per group, the default requirement of at least seven replicates for Cook’s count replacement is not met. Gene-level Cook’s filtering can therefore leave p values unavailable, even though no biological sample is removed. Missing adjusted p values caused by independent filtering are distinguished from these unavailable nominal tests.


Quality assessment and displays
Sample summaries include total assigned gene counts, detected genes, size factors, and mitochondrial and ribosomal RNA count fractions. These fractions summarize the supplied count matrix and do not replace read-level quality assessment. PCA uses a blind variance-stabilizing transformation and the 500 most variable retained genes, centered without variance scaling. Heatmap rows are standardized only for visualization. Neither PCA nor the top-ranked heatmap is an independent validation dataset.

This analysis keeps age, genotype, and exposure distinct and estimates ozone-versus-filtered-air contrasts within each age-by-genotype stratum. (Nakamya et al. 2025)
Gene-level inference is complete for 24 libraries. The results below are read from the completed contrast tables. Read-level QC, quantification QC, and figures are displayed when their corresponding completed outputs are available.

Read-level QC and adapter decisions
The initial fastp screen examines the first 200,000 read pairs per library. This is a bounded, position-dependent QC sample, not a random subsample or an all-read quality assessment. Adapter evidence from paired-read overlap determines whether at least 0.5% of sampled reads require adapter trimming. For a flagged library, fastp then processes the complete paired FASTQ files to produce derived adapter-trimmed input for quantification. Quality filtering, length filtering, poly-G trimming, and duplicate removal are disabled in this workflow. Original downloaded FASTQ files are preserved.
Full-read fastp reports, where trimming is performed, remain available separately from the initial sampled-QC reports. Q30 percentages in the initial screen must therefore be interpreted as sampled-read summaries. Adapter-related pair removals are counted separately in the full-run records, including short adapter-dimer pairs; disabled quality and length filters do not imply that every original pair survives adapter processing. Quantification integrity is assessed from the complete library’s Salmon outputs and reference-to-transcript mapping, rather than inferred from that screen alone.


Transcript quantification and gene-level import
The workflow uses Salmon selective alignment against GENCODE M25 mouse transcripts with the whole GRCm38 primary genome as decoys. Library orientation is detected automatically, and sequence- and GC-bias models are enabled. Quantification uses all input read pairs or their complete derived adapter-trimmed equivalents. (Patro et al. 2017)
Tximport summarizes estimated transcript fragments to genes with countsFromAbundance="no", preserving sample-specific abundance-weighted effective gene lengths. DESeqDataSetFromTximport includes the corresponding gene-length offsets in the count model. Estimated fragments and TPM are exported separately; TPM values are not supplied as raw counts to DESeq2. Genes require at least ten rounded estimated fragments in at least three of the 24 libraries, using a rule independent of the group labels. (Soneson et al. 2015; Love et al. 2014)
The mouse reference does not provide allele-specific quantification of the human APOE3 and APOE4 replacement sequences. Genotype groups come from the experimental metadata. No APOE-allele expression estimate or verified allele-specific mapping performance is claimed. Counts aligned at the mouse Apoe/humanized APOE replacement locus are not interpreted as validated allele- or locus-specific expression measurements.


Four stratified contrasts and the global ozone test
The full negative-binomial model is ~age * genotype * exposure. Dispersions are estimated using all 24 libraries. Equivalent group-factor reparameterizations make each planned within-stratum ozone-versus-filtered-air effect a single coefficient for Wald testing and apeglm shrinkage. Original Wald maximum-likelihood effects and p values are preserved; shrunken effects are additional estimates for interpretation and visualization. (Love et al. 2014; Zhu et al. 2019)
Benjamini–Hochberg adjustment is reported within each of the four prespecified contrasts. A supplementary column, padj_across_four_strata, adjusts the combined p-value family across all four contrasts. These columns answer different multiplicity questions and are shown separately. Their discovery sets need not be nested: a different ranked p-value family can increase or decrease the adjusted value for an individual test. This p-value adjustment does not pool animals into a single exposure group. A global likelihood-ratio test compares the full model with ~age * genotype, using four degrees of freedom to ask whether adding exposure-related coefficients improves the fit. Its gene-level BH adjustment forms a separate family. The global test has no single signed ozone effect and is not used as a signed preranked-enrichment statistic. (Benjamini and Hochberg 1995)
Cook’s filtering remains enabled. The fixed count prefilter is followed by BH adjustment of the valid tests; adaptive independent filtering is disabled. Numerically nonconverged coefficient fits and genes with zero counts in all six animals of a stratum are flagged, with their exposure-test p values withheld before BH adjustment. Global full- and reduced-model convergence is checked separately. No unverified library batch or RIN covariate is invented. Evidence that ozone responses differ between strata requires an appropriate interaction comparison; differing numbers of significant genes alone are insufficient.


Relationship to the original publication
This is an independent raw-read reanalysis. The original publication used HISAT2/featureCounts and selected exposure-associated genes with nominal p < 0.05 and absolute log₂FC > 0.1. Here, Salmon/tximport quantification, the factorial count model, and BH FDR < 0.05 define a different analysis. Discovery counts must therefore not be described as reproducing the publication’s nominal-p gene lists. (Nakamya et al. 2025)

text:
Interpretation and limits
The stratified comparisons estimate hippocampal tissue-level differences in the original mouse experiment. Sample numbers remain three per exposure group within each stratum even though the full model borrows information across the complete design. Genotype and starting-age labels do not make these libraries interchangeable with the PM cortex or hypothalamus studies. Mouse-reference quantification, the unprovided batch/RIN covariates, and the deposited strain inconsistency remain limitations. No spatially resolved ozone-response measurement or cell-type-specific exposure effect is generated by this pipeline.
Unequal discovery counts across the strata do not by themselves establish that APOE4 or older age increases susceptibility. The global four-degree-of-freedom test assesses whether any exposure-related term improves the model; it does not isolate an age-by-exposure or genotype-by-exposure interaction. Such a claim would require a corresponding interaction contrast and its own uncertainty and multiplicity assessment.
GO analyses of completed signed Wald contrasts, when available, are presented separately on the enrichment page. Their addition does not convert the global LRT into a directional pathway analysis or justify pooling contrasts from different brain regions and exposures.

title: Response heterogeneity and pathway architecture
text:
The primary ozone contrasts quantify exposure-associated differences within each age/APOE stratum. A significant result in one stratum and a nonsignificant result in another does not establish different responses. This secondary analysis directly tests whether the O₃-versus-filtered-air effect differs by age or genotype. It uses the same 24 animals and 18,537 retained genes, without adding independent biological observations. These are new exploratory analyses of Nakamya et al.’s deposit, distinct from reproduction of the authors’ results. Nakamya et al. (2025)
Bulk tissue effects can reflect expression regulation, cell composition, or vascular material. Neither an interaction coefficient nor a GO label identifies a responding cell type. Methods
The analysis reuses the measured-count matrix and registered hypothalamic cell annotations underlying the linked 3D viewer. Exact string cell identifiers join the annotations to matrix rows; Ensembl gene identifiers determine column order. Duplicate or missing identifiers cause an explicit failure. All selected cells and all measured genes enter the summaries. The source atlas classes and CCF substructure labels remain unchanged.
For each class and substructure, composition is its cell count divided by all selected reference cells. For every measured gene, the mean is the arithmetic mean of linear imaging counts across all cells in the group, including measured zeros. A positive cell has a measured count strictly greater than zero; the detection fraction is the positive-cell count divided by that group’s cell count. No normalization to bulk RNA-seq units, log transformation, or expression imputation is applied to these summaries.
The Tll1 class plot includes all classes. The anatomical display shows the 15 highest detection fractions among substructures containing at least 100 selected cells; this rule limits the display, not the exported analysis. Complete tables retain every substructure, including small groups and unassigned labels. Substructures include nuclei and other anatomical areas, so they are not all distinct nuclei.
These are descriptive measurements from one donor. No cell-level differential test, clustering, p value, confidence interval, or exposure model is fitted. The cell count does not provide independent animal replication. The selected registered hemisphere also does not establish an unbiased whole-organ cell composition. Atlas class names are inherited taxonomy labels; a regional name within a class label does not replace a cell’s deposited HY location.

text:
Software and backend separation
The recorded Python environment is Python 3.14.3 on macOS arm64. The Python package inventory and environment record accompany the report. They document the environment used here; the package list alone is not a complete operating-system, binary or transitive-dependency lockfile.

R 4.5.2 is available separately from Python. The scripts prepend the project-local .r-library to the R library search path. Required direct R packages are limma, edgeR, tximport, DESeq2, apeglm, jsonlite and, for the independent cross-check, BiocParallel. Their Bioconductor dependencies must also be installed. R session records preserve the complete loaded-package context; see the miRNA session and independent DESeq2 session.
Ozone processing additionally requires salmon, fastp, aria2c and Rscript on PATH. aria2c is used by the annotation downloader even though the transcript/genome downloader has a curl fallback. Exposure downloads use curl. Rendering requires the Quarto CLI and ipykernel. The local viewer requires a browser supporting WebGL and gzip DecompressionStream; its Plotly library and expression files are served locally, without a runtime CDN dependency.
For a new Python environment, the recorded package inventory can be installed as follows. This prepares software only; the original data, R packages, external tools and references remain separate prerequisites.
python3.14 -m venv .venv-analysis
.venv-analysis/bin/python -m pip install -r requirements-analysis.txt
The commands below assume the shell is in the repository root and use the existing .venv-analysis interpreter. Scripts resolve data paths from their project location. A rendered HTML copy alone is not a replacement for the complete repository, source data and environments needed for a rebuild.

title: Data, code, and reproducibility
text:
Regenerate the study analyses
The execution runner provides a readable plan before execution:
.venv-analysis/bin/python scripts/run_analysis.py --stage all --cpus 4 --dry-run
.venv-analysis/bin/python scripts/run_analysis.py --stage all --cpus 4
The full runner follows this order: hypothalamus, cortex, miRNA, ozone, enrichment, spatial viewer, descriptive spatial-reference summaries, then report. It does not install tools or download the original study collection. It refits the processed-data analyses; it should not be used merely to refresh HTML. Run only one ozone pipeline instance in a project workspace so that concurrent processes do not write the same quantification directories.
Individual commands make each backend and dependency explicit:
# Seven-sample hypothalamus analysis, including all seven leave-one-out fits.
.venv-analysis/bin/python scripts/analyze_hypothalamus.py --cpus 4

# Eight-sample cingulate-cortex PM-versus-PBS analysis.
.venv-analysis/bin/python scripts/analyze_cortex.py --workers 4

# Nine miRNA arrays; this command invokes the R/limma backend.
.venv-analysis/bin/python scripts/analyze_mirna.py

# GO-BP analyses for the completed hypothalamus and cortex gene-level contrasts.
.venv-analysis/bin/python scripts/analyze_enrichment.py --threads 4
Hypothalamus uses at most six Python inference workers; cortex accepts one to six workers. GSEA uses at most four threads. The hypothalamus --skip-sensitivity option deliberately omits the leave-one-out fits; the standard viewer rebuild expects their saved primary-hit stability table, so the complete default run is the reproducibility route documented here.
Each study writes to its own results/ directory. Count filters, sample selections, MLE versus shrunken effects, missing-p handling, normalized matrices and figure captions are recorded in the corresponding hypothalamus, cortex and miRNA method files. PCA is descriptive: hypothalamus uses a design-informed VST, whereas cortex uses a blind VST. Both use mean-centered, unscaled gene features; neither PCA determines sample removal.
The enrichment command uses exact mouse symbols and unambiguous GAF synonyms. Its ORA universe requires finite adjusted DE p-values; its GSEA rank requires finite original p-values and signed Wald statistics while retaining finite-p genes with missing adjusted p-values from independent filtering. Rank exclusions and mapping decisions are part of the reproducibility record. miRNA identifiers are not submitted as mRNA genes for GO enrichment.

Independent implementation check
The optional R DESeq2 cross-check is separate from the primary PyDESeq2 workflow:
.venv-analysis/bin/python scripts/validate_hypothalamus_deseq2.py

# Regenerate only its comparison tables from the existing R fit.
.venv-analysis/bin/python scripts/validate_hypothalamus_deseq2.py --reuse-R-fit
The saved check uses the same seven samples, count filter and 19,452 finite-p hypotheses, with identical 159-gene Cook’s filtering. Numerical agreement is close. R finds twelve FDR hits compared with the primary eleven; the additional threshold crossing is Tnrc6c (R adjusted p = 0.0399; Python = 0.0521). Tll1 remains significant in both implementations (approximately 0.00330 and 0.00350). This is an implementation comparison, not independent biological replication, and it does not replace the primary result or its sample-sensitivity limitation. The R code, comparison code and gene-level differences are available.

title: Data, code, and reproducibility
text:
Ozone: stages and resumability
The ozone workflow starts from the original paired reads. prepare obtains and verifies GENCODE M25/GRCm38 references, creates transcript-to-gene mappings and full-genome decoys, and obtains true gene-type annotations from the GTF. index builds the Salmon index. qc examines the first 200,000 pairs per library and records the adapter-trimming rule. quant processes complete libraries, applying adapter trimming where indicated. de imports all 24 quantifications with effective-length offsets and runs the fixed factorial R model. figures and enrichment consume completed statistical results.
# Complete raw-read workflow; use a budget appropriate to the local computer.
.venv-analysis/bin/python scripts/ozone_pipeline.py --stage all --cpus 12

# Resume quantification after an interrupted process has stopped.
.venv-analysis/bin/python scripts/ozone_pipeline.py --stage quant --cpus 12

# These stages require all 24 completed quantifications / statistical results.
.venv-analysis/bin/python scripts/ozone_pipeline.py --stage de
.venv-analysis/bin/python scripts/ozone_pipeline.py --stage figures
.venv-analysis/bin/python scripts/ozone_pipeline.py --stage enrichment
The --cpus budget governs indexing and quantification. At eight or more CPUs, quantification uses two concurrent workers, each with half the integer budget; otherwise it uses one worker. Raw-read fastp QC uses two threads, and the enrichment stage uses four. Original FASTQ files are never modified. Derived trimmed reads are removed after successful quantification while the trimming reports are retained.
The index and per-library ozone_quant_complete.json markers allow completed work to be reused. They are local checkpoints, not a mechanism for changing references or analysis parameters in place. Preserve the associated quantification files and source hashes; changed inputs or settings require a separately reviewed rebuild. A resumed process should not be launched alongside another active pipeline instance.
Current stage information is in pipeline_status.json. Its complete field refers to the selected stage; successful quant does not imply that differential expression or enrichment has finished. Per-library logs and quantifications remain under results/ozone/. The ozone results page distinguishes available QC from completed inference and does not fill missing stages with simulated results.
The full statistical model crosses age, genotype and exposure. A fixed count prefilter defines the candidate genes; adaptive independent filtering is disabled for this analysis. Numerical convergence flags are checked before the final BH adjustment, and failed shrinkage estimates are withheld. Within-stratum Wald tests, a supplementary pooled-four-contrast BH family and the separate four-degree-of-freedom global LRT answer different questions. The reference cannot validate human APOE allele-specific quantification. A source strain annotation that differs for one library is retained as a metadata limitation, rather than being converted into a wholly confounded genotype adjustment.

title: Data, code, and reproducibility
text:
Regenerate the measured-reference viewer
The viewer builder requires the downloaded Zhuang reference inputs and completed hypothalamus count, effect and leave-one-out files. The reference donor is fixed to ABCA-2; changing donors requires a separately named analysis rather than overwriting this release.
.venv-analysis/bin/python scripts/build_spatial_viewer.py --dataset Zhuang-ABCA-2
This writes the local expression payloads, coordinates, geometry and Plotly library into docs/assets/viewer/, and data checks and static figures into results/spatial_viewer/. The versioned index.html, viewer.js and viewer.css frontend files remain part of the repository. The extraction cache is reused only when its recorded cell and gene identifiers match the current selection.
The published view contains all 37,811 selected hypothalamic reference cells and 1,122 measured genes. A uniform regional multiplier transfers each eligible bulk effect to the same reference positions. It does not estimate exposed single-cell expression, alter cell abundance or create a spatially measured exposure response. The model and coordinate checks, validation record, and viewer instructions accompany the assets.
The descriptive reference summaries reuse the validated viewer cache and keep all measured genes, classes and substructures:
.venv-analysis/bin/python scripts/analyze_spatial_reference.py
Measured-reference composition and expression summaries contain no cell-level exposure tests or animal-level replication claims.

title: Data, code, and reproducibility
section: Render the report without refitting models
text:
Render the report without refitting models
Quarto renders completed tables, figures and the local viewer. The rendering helper copies eligible outputs into docs/downloads/ and docs/assets/figures/, bundles source scripts and provenance, and records the Python environment. It does not call the statistical analysis scripts.
# Copy the existing outputs and source bundles without rendering HTML.
.venv-analysis/bin/python scripts/render_docs.py --prepare-only

# Render the complete website, or only this page.
.venv-analysis/bin/python scripts/render_docs.py
.venv-analysis/bin/python scripts/render_docs.py --page reproducibility.qmd

# Inspect the rendered site on this computer.
.venv-analysis/bin/python -m http.server 8000 --bind 127.0.0.1 --directory docs/_site
The site is then available at http://127.0.0.1:8000/. The helper registers the local omics-analysis kernel and supplies its Python/Jupyter paths to Quarto. The output directory is docs/_site/. Rendering does not require repeating RNA-seq quantification, fitting models, rebuilding the spatial atlas or downloading source files.
Downloadable original study files can be restored or resumed with the exposure downloader and spatial downloader, using their saved manifests. scripts/status.py reports exposure-download state; scripts/download_spatial_atlas.py --status reports atlas-download state. Full input validation and per-analysis validation records describe the checks performed, while preserving the distinction between computational checks and biological validation.
The QMD and frontend source archive contains the report authoring files. Restore its docs/ tree within the complete repository when editing; the archive does not include original omics data or the generated expression payloads.
